plain: An Australian intelligence report from 1971 is said to show that the United States quietly studied UFOs and tried to learn how to control gravity in the 1950s. Jesse Michels brings it up again and again. He says it was written by Harry Turner, whom he calls the head of the nuclear division of the Joint Intelligence Organisation, an Australian spy agency he describes as "basically Australia's CIA", though once he says he is not sure of Turner's exact post. As Michels quotes it, the document reads: "A more astounding decision on the part of the US government was to allocate considerable funds to investigate gravity and a means of controlling gravity." According to Michels, it names famous physicists such as J. Robert Oppenheimer, Edward Teller and Freeman Dyson among the people involved, and it says Turner urged Australia to put more effort into UFO research. Michels also says it describes a research institute at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, run by a businessman named Agnew Bahnson, as an academic outpost of the CIA studying anti-gravity, and that it calls Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, a public relations front. The researcher Ross Coulthart gives the date as 1972 and says the report covers the recovery of crashed craft and a UFO "flying squad". The researcher Eric Weinstein also cites it, and Michels says the UFO whistleblower David Grusch quotes it often. If it says what they say, a foreign ally was recording secret American work on gravity and UFOs decades ago.
